extracted.intended_audience: Directors and Heads of Communication; government communicators and GCS leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Nationwide UK Government Communication Service operating model and guidance for building, leading and running communications teams, and for planning and delivering government communications and campaigns. Covers mandatory policies, team design, capability, ethics, procurement, data protection, evaluation and crisis response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with GCS Strategy and Government Communication Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: All departmental or organisational communication plans must reflect the strategic priorities in the Government Communication Plan and the GCS Strategy 2022-25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Plans must include clear metrics to support delivery of cross-government and organisational objectives, approved by the organisation’s board (or equivalent). Use the GCS Strategy and Government Communication Plan as the 'what' and MCOM policies/guidance as the 'how'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership objective for SCS leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: The specified leadership objective must be included in annual performance and development plans of all SCS leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Include the quoted objective: “GCS SCS to play an active role in championing the three pillars of the GCS Strategy 2022-25 by promoting collaboration, increasing efficiency and innovation, supporting great people and raising professional standards, and contributing to the delivery of the GCS strategy commitments.” Support through leadership capability framework and targeted skills development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team design principles and roles/accountabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads of Communication must clearly set out roles and accountabilities (e.g. in an organogram) and apply design principles when structuring teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Ensure tiered accountability so decision ownership is clear; work collaboratively to achieve clear, simple and consistent communication; manage duplication and minimise complexity; keep processes simple, proportionate and user-focused; define roles to suit activity needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-disciplinary approach and seven MCOM disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication teams should apply a multi-disciplinary approach and represent the core seven MCOM disciplines to differing degrees depending on need, size and focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: The seven disciplines are Data & Insight, Digital, External Affairs, Internal Communication, Media, Marketing, Strategic Communication. This does not require seven siloed teams; skills should exist somewhere in the team and be available to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital team design principles and core functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital teams should include generalist digital experts and specialists; structure around four core functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Four core functions are Digital Strategy & Leadership; Data and insight analysis; Technical content creation (graphic design, animation, videography, photography); Copywriting, editing, channel management & strategic platform publishing. Full Digital discipline guide available from GCS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heads of Discipline (HoD/DHoD) duties and time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each MCOM discipline has a Head and Deputy Head expected to spend 20% of their time developing their discipline’s network and capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: HoDs/DHoDs build capability, share best practice, facilitate cross-government collaboration and raise standards. They are appointed through a light-touch open recruitment process for two-year posts. Directors/Heads should support inclusion of their 20% contribution within PDPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for HoDs in Personal Development Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads of Communication should enable HoDs/DHoDs to include their 20% discipline contribution within Personal Development Plans (PDPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: DoCs and HoCs should work collaboratively with discipline networks and champion the HoD/DHoD roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation-wide communications accountability and GovS011 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors or Heads of Communication are responsible for managing the communication function across their organisation and for ensuring compliance with Functional Standard GovS011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should/Must: Directors and Heads must ensure their whole organisation, including ALBs and embedded communicators, complies with GovS011 and aligns to GCS vision and strategy. They should have oversight of relevant recruitment and ensure use of standards is embedded in business plans and annual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALB / Sponsor department collaboration principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for establishing collaborative partnerships between ALBs and sponsoring departments to remove duplication and enable integrated working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Where part of an ALB cluster, remove duplication and promote integrated working; consider sharing services across groups or GCS; sponsor departments should quality-assure ALBs without inhibiting autonomy and encourage access to GCS learning offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded communicators oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads of Communication should establish links, reporting lines and oversight of embedded communications staff outside the core function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Know how many embedded communicators work within the organisation, what they do and their skill levels; ensure embedded communicators deliver work consistent with GCS/organisational standards and have access to career and skills development; seek approval before recruiting embedded roles to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) alignment and action
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders should review and align their people plans with the GCS EDI Action Plan to improve diversity and inclusion across teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Apply actions from the EDI Action Plan and Civil Service Diversity & Inclusion Strategy; build and develop diverse teams across the UK so communications reflect the communities served.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCS Location Strategy and regional careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads should incorporate the GCS Location Strategy and promote careers across the UK, advertising roles outside London by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Support team members across sites to feel part of GCS community with access to training, development and career opportunities; consider location strategy in team building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce planning and GCS Data Collection participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders should support the annual GCS Data Collection for workforce planning and skills development and nominate representatives to ensure timely and complete returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Provide support for returning data for all organisations they lead and nominate representatives to ensure Sponsored Organisations provide information on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building capability, talent identification and talent grids
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads must take responsibility for building capability and talent, using career pathways and talent approaches to attract, develop and retain communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Ensure L&D is aligned to organisational capability needs and GCS Data Collection analysis; actively identify talent, complete talent grids and champion GCS talent schemes; use apprenticeships and leadership offers to develop diverse talent pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the GCS Career Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicators should use the Career Framework to clarify skills, capability and experience needed by grade and to record development goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Communicators use the Career Framework to discuss learning and development and record goals in PDPs. Leaders should encourage its use to support career progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory learning and development days / CPD
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of GCS must engage in 4–5 days of training per year, equivalent to at least 30 Continuing Professional Development points, and record this in PDPs and GCS Connect profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: L&D engagement is mandatory and should be reflected in PDPs. Leaders should champion GCS Advance and foster a culture that prioritises learning and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the Communications Functional Standard (GovS011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads must have a plan to demonstrate compliance with the mandatory elements ('shalls') of GovS011 and embed use of the standards into business plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Statements about use of functional standards should be included in annual reports and Accounting Officer system statements where relevant. Directors must demonstrate how they meet mandatory elements in line with business needs and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in GCS governance boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors of Communication and Heads of Communications for ALBs should participate in cross-government boards that feed into the GCS Board and contribute corporately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Actively participate and make corporate contributions to the delivery of GCS Strategy Commitments and cross-government working groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety and ethics adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: All government communicators must carry out work objectively and without political bias, in accordance with the Civil Service Code and propriety guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Ensure all communicators are clear on propriety and ethics guidance, responsibilities and how to raise concerns. Complete mandatory propriety and ethics training (mandatory for departments, strongly advised for ALBs); follow guidance on propriety in digital and social media; leaders must ensure regular reminders of duties and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI policy and safe use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of generative AI must follow the GCS generative AI policy and relevant government guidance, with attention to accuracy, inclusivity and bias mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Directors and Heads must ensure teams have read and follow GCS generative AI policy and government frameworks; ensure use is in accordance with latest guidance; teams should complete GCS Advance AI training before using generative AI; refer to Annex A of the GCS policy for links to wider AI assurance guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement, advertising/marketing spend controls and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to GCS procurement policies and the Cabinet Office spending controls for advertising, marketing and communications (AMC) spend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Campaigns/projects with planned communications expenditure of £100,000+ in a financial year must follow the three-stage approval process and technical business case which GCS processes with a 21 calendar day SLA (not applicable during recess). Use approved government procurement frameworks and guidance from the Commercial Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital brand safety using the SAFER framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SAFER framework principles to assess digital environments and adopt a risk-based approach to government advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Directors must ensure Campaign Team leads use the SAFER framework (safety, appropriate environments, freedom of speech, ethics, risks and responsibilities) to demonstrate responsible use of taxpayers’ money and protect the UK Government brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data handling and Data Protection Act / GDPR compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications work must conform to the Data Protection Act 2018 and leaders must ensure understanding of the eight data protection principles and GDPR obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Ensure awareness of when to complete a DPIA, adopt 'privacy by design', consult the organisation’s Data Protection Officer, and follow ICO guidance. Summarised principles include lawful processing, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, rights of individuals, retention minimisation, security and safe transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Marketing, Programmatic RTB and platform-specific privacy guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaign teams must demonstrate lawful basis for direct marketing within DPIAs, adopt 'Least Data by Default' for programmatic real-time bidding, and follow Facebook-related privacy/cookie guidance when sharing data with platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Campaign leads should consult DPO and GCS guidance (ICO Direct Marketing campaign guidance, Compliant use of Programmatic Real-Time-Bidding, GCS website development GDPR guidance) and follow specific steps to ensure compliant use of RTB and platform data-sharing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible communications and Equality Act obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure communications are accessible and inclusive, meeting GCS accessibility standards and making reasonable adjustments where communications affect disabled people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Read Accessible Communications guidance; consider BSL where ministerial announcements affect Deaf BSL users and follow GCS guidance on BSL content. Accessibility standards help ensure content is inclusive and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: HMG brand and identity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications must comply with HMG Government identity and branding guidance; only authorised organisations may use Royal Coat of Arms and associated insignia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must: Directors and Heads must ensure all communications activities comply with HMG branding guidance on the GCS website and protect official recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: OASIS campaign planning principles
rubrics_metrics.description: All government campaigns should be developed and delivered according to the Guide to campaign planning: OASIS and view activities in the context of a wider campaign with clear objectives and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Use OASIS principles to create a compelling narrative over time to deliver defined and measurable outcomes; embed evaluation and link campaign design to strategic objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework for Ethical Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the Framework for Ethical Innovation to assess ethical and legal implications of emerging technologies and data use in communications from project scoping onwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Directors and Heads must ensure teams have read and apply the framework for innovation projects; be aware of cross-government policies (HMG Generative AI Framework, Responsible Technology Adoption, GCS policies, SAFER); be clear on processes for raising concerns or barriers to upholding obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Cycle and continuous evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation is a continuous six-step process and should be embedded from the start of campaign planning to measure impact and enable learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Directors and Heads should ensure teams implement the Evaluation Cycle, emphasise continuous learning, share insights across teams and draw links with OASIS, COM-B and Theory of Change. Use digital techniques for real-time evaluation and adapt to audience needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communications preparedness and STOP framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors of Communication must prepare and manage crisis communications for risks their department owns, using the Crisis Communications Operating Model and the STOP framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must/Should: Be familiar with the Crisis Communications Operating Model; use the Crisis Communication Planning Guide and the STOP framework (Strategy, Tactics, Organisation, People) to create contingency plans; embed comms into crisis management structures and ensure roles and responsibilities are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mis- and disinformation: apply RESIST 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads should follow the RESIST 3 framework to reduce the impact of mis- and disinformation when communicating in contested environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Develop expertise to understand adversary disinformation techniques and apply RESIST 3 guidance as part of strategic communications planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: PITCH toolkit for international strategic communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the PITCH toolkit to develop and deliver credible, proactive and effective global communication campaigns for international audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Directors/Heads working with international audiences should be familiar with PITCH tools and best practices, use its Annex A checklist for campaigns and read it alongside RESIST 3 for strategic communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioural science and COM-B model usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a behavioural approach using the COM-B model to ensure communications are audience-centred and effective for behaviour change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Directors/Heads ensure familiarity with GCS guidance on behaviour change communications and COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, Motivation, Behaviour) and use it to identify barriers to behaviour change systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer marketing governance and reputational checks
rubrics_metrics.description: When using influencers, ensure rigorous checks and transparency to avoid reputational risk and erosion of public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Follow Guidelines for Influencer Marketing (member-only content); conduct rigorous checks managed by an agency as per RIPA where applicable; apply SAFER principles; consult organisational influencer marketing guidance before campaign activity goes live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow discipline-specific models and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors and Heads should use models/guidance provided for each of the seven MCOM disciplines according to organisational needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should: Refer to discipline guides for External Affairs, Marketing, Internal Communication, Media, Strategic Communication, Data & Insight and Digital Communication and apply relevant best practice and skills guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Media Monitoring Unit (MMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access MMU subscription services for 24/7 media briefings, transcripts and embargoed stories to inform communications work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All: Departments and ALBs may subscribe to MMU for daily monitoring, verbatim transcripts and ad hoc interview/report summaries. Contact mmu@cabinetoffice.gov.uk for monitoring requests.
